To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the scattering efficiency Qscat of nonspherical Chebyszhev particles is larger than that of spheres, the absorption efficiency is larger than that for spheres, the single-scattered fraction is smaller than that for spheres and the asymmetry factor is smaller than that of spheres.
nonspherical particles have larger Qabs, smaller g, and smaller ω than their spherical counterparts.
nonspherical particles with refractive indexes in the range 1.5−i ≤ m ≤ 1.5+i are more absorbing, less backscattering, and more forward scattering than spherical ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the behavior of the single-scattering properties of rotationally symmetric Chebyshev particle models.
the scattering characteristics of nonspherical particles, with emphasis on the behavior of Qsca, Qabs, ω, g, and β for randomly oriented nonspherical Chebyszhev particles of different shape.

the scattering properties of nonspherical particles, which is important for understanding light scattering from atmospheric particles, especially ice particles in cirrus clouds, and from interplanetary and interstellar dust.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nonspherical scattering is more complex and less understood than spherical scattering, and that the scattering behavior of nonspherical particles is not easily predictable.
, in general, the scattering properties of nonspherical particles differ considerably from those of spherical particles.
, on the average, nonspherical particles scatter more light than do spherical particles of the same volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the scattering behavior of nonspherical Chebyeshev particles can be very different from that of spheres, and that the shape-averaged scattering quantities are in general not the same as the size-averaged ones.
nonsphericity increases Qsca and Qabs, decreases g and increases β.
nonspherical particles tend to scatter more efficiently, and less selectively, in the forward direction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scattering properties of nonspherical particles are quite different from those of the corresponding spheres, even for relatively small size parameters. © The Author(s) 2020.
